MeAndQi TCM education center BL23
PMC11353071 (back-shu points biomechanics study; methods give T-level + 1.5 B-cun)

standard_landmarks: Level of the lower border of the L2 spinous process, 1.5 cun lateral to posterior midline (same level as GV4). Back-shu line: 1.5 B-cun (about 1.5 thumb-widths / 2 finger-widths) lateral to the posterior midline, measured from the lower border of the spinous process of the named vertebra. WHO surface landmarks: T3 spinous process = line joining medial ends of the scapular spines; T7 = line joining inferior scapular angles (arms at sides); T12 = midpoint between inferior scapular angle and top of iliac crest; L4 = line joining top of iliac crests; S2 = line joining inferior borders of the PSISs.
corrected_location: On the low back, about one and a half thumb-widths out from the spine, at the level of the second lumbar vertebra: roughly halfway between where the lowest rib meets the spine and the top of the hip bones.
notes: App's 'level with the bottom of the rib cage' is loose; also inconsistent with BL22 text ('just below the rib cage' for a point that is higher than BL23). Midway rule derived from WHO landmarks T12 and L4 (L2 is midway between them). Independence caveat: TCM Wiki, Master Tung and MeAndQi all follow the standard Chinese-textbook wording and are not fully independent of each other or of the WHO/China national standard; WHO is the separate consensus reference.

standard_landmarks: Level of lower border of T3 spinous process, 1.5 cun lateral to midline. WHO defines T3 as the line between the medial ends of the two scapular spines (standing, arms at sides).
corrected_location: On the upper back, about one and a half thumb-widths out from the spine, level with the line joining the inner ends of the ridges (spines) that run across the two shoulder blades (third thoracic vertebra).
notes: 'Top of the shoulder blades' is ambiguous: the upper tip of the scapula is higher than the scapular spine root that defines T3. (The superior-angle-at-T2 statement is general anatomy, not from the sources I opened.) Independence caveat: TCM Wiki, Master Tung and MeAndQi all follow the standard Chinese-textbook wording and are not fully independent of each other or of the WHO/China national standard; WHO is the separate consensus reference.

standard_landmarks: Lower border of T9 spinous process, 1.5 cun lateral to midline. WHO: the bottom tips (inferior angles) of the scapulae are at T7, so BL18 is two vertebrae below that line.
corrected_location: On the mid-back, about one and a half thumb-widths out from the spine, at the level of the 9th thoracic vertebra, which is two vertebrae (roughly a hand's width) below the line joining the bottom tips of the shoulder blades.
notes: Level (T9) and 1.5 cun are right. The 'two finger-widths below shoulder blades' measure likely understates the gap (two vertebrae is about 3 cun by my estimate of ~1.5 cun per vertebra; that spacing figure is NOT from a source I opened). Suggest dropping or changing the finger measure; flag for owner. Independence caveat: TCM Wiki, Master Tung and MeAndQi all follow the standard Chinese-textbook wording and are not fully independent of each other or of the WHO/China national standard; WHO is the separate consensus reference.

standard_landmarks: Level of the 1st posterior sacral foramen, 1.5 cun lateral to the median sacral crest (WHO: same level as BL31). WHO defines S2 as the line joining the lower borders of the two PSISs (the visible dimples), so the dimple level is S2 = BL28/BL32 level, one segment BELOW BL27.
controversy: None found among sources on level (S1 foramen). Dimple-level wording is my deduction from WHO's S2 landmark definition.
corrected_location: On the lower back over the sacrum, about one and a half thumb-widths out from the midline, roughly one thumb-width above the level of the dimples above the buttocks (at the level of the first sacral hole).
notes: App says BL27 is 'at the level of the dimples'; the dimples mark S2 which is BL28. 'One thumb-width above' is an approximation of S1-S2 spacing (not from a source). Independence caveat: TCM Wiki, Master Tung and MeAndQi all follow the standard Chinese-textbook wording and are not fully independent of each other or of the WHO/China national standard; WHO is the separate consensus reference.

standard_landmarks: Outer side of the foot, in the depression proximal (behind) the 5th metatarsophalangeal joint, i.e. just behind the HEAD of the 5th metatarsal, at the border of red and white skin. (TCM Wiki: posterior and inferior to the head.) The BASE of the 5th metatarsal is the BL64 (Jinggu) landmark.
corrected_location: On the outer edge of the foot, in the hollow just behind the knuckle where the little toe joins the foot (the rounded head of the little toe's long bone), where the darker skin of the top of the foot meets the paler skin of the sole.
notes: App says 'behind the base of the little toe's long bone', which read literally is the proximal end of the metatarsal (BL64 area), not BL65. Could be an ambiguous phrase for 'base of the little toe', but it is wrong as written. Independence caveat: TCM Wiki, Master Tung and MeAndQi all follow the standard Chinese-textbook wording and are not fully independent of each other or of the WHO/China national standard; WHO is the separate consensus reference.

standard_landmarks: WHO: posterior neck at the level of the upper border of the C2 spinous process, in the depression on the outer side of the trapezius. TCM Wiki/Master Tung/MeAndQi: 1.3 cun lateral to the midline (GV15 Yamen), 0.5 cun above the posterior hairline, on the lateral edge of trapezius.
